keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page says the state 'ruled modern Wuwei' and names no prefecture and no Hexi Corridor; Liangzhou in a 100 km circle is the researcher's reading. The 1015 and 1016 events of the page are drawn as occupation by the Tanguts and the end of the state.

ledger.note: 906: Xiliangfu 'established in 906' at Liangzhou (modern Wuwei). The page names no founder; the Guiyi page has Liangzhou slip away from the Guiyi in 881-882, so the land came from nobody.
1001: Panluozhi comes to power at Liangzhou. 'Panluozhi came to power in 1001.' The page gives no month.

ledger.note: 1003: Li Jiqian occupies Liangzhou. 'Li Jiqian occupied Liangzhou but lost it after a Tibetan ambush' (no month).
1004: Siduodu succeeds. 'He was assassinated by Tanguts in 1004, and his brother Siduodu succeeded him.'

region.text: Liangzhou (modern Wuwei in Gansu): the only land the Xiliangfu page names

ledger.note: 1004: the Tangut occupation ends. The Timeline of the Tanguts has Li Jiqian die in battle against the Tibetan state of Xiliangfu on 6 January 1004 (the Li Jiqian page gives 26 January 1004, 'aged 40-41'); the Xiliangfu page says Panluozhi was 'assassinated by Tanguts in 1004' and his brother Siduodu succeeded. Neither page says when the ambush that ended the occupation fell, so the end is dated by Li Jiqian's death.

ledger.note: 1015: the Tanguts capture Liangzhou. 'Tanguts captured Liangzhou' in 1015 (Xiliangfu page); the Timeline of the Tanguts: 'Dingnan Jiedushi takes Liangzhou from Xiliangfu but is ousted by the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom'. The Western Xia page does not mention the 1015 conquest.

region.text: Liangzhou (modern Wuwei in Gansu): the only land the Xiliangfu page names

ledger.note: 1016: Xiliangfu 'disestablished'. The infobox lists 1016 as the end and 'succeeded by Western Xia and Tsongkha'; the lead has it 'conquered by the Tanguts of Western Xia and Uyghurs in 1015 and 1016'. The Western Xia page and the Timeline of the Tanguts have the Tibetan Xiliangfu annexed by Li Yuanhao only in 1032, so the Tibetan confederation may have outlived the loss of Liangzhou; the year 1016 follows the Xiliangfu page. Who held Liangzhou between 1016 and 1032 is not on any page.

notes: New state (Cliopatria has no row); requested by ea-04-b as 'Xiliangfu (Tibetan state at Liangzhou)' and counted by the ganzhou-kingdom, guiyi-circuit and tibetans dossiers. Open points: (1) the Xiliangfu page ends the state in 1016 while the Western Xia page and the Timeline of the Tanguts annex it in 1032; the dossier ends in 1016 and a gap-filler could extend the Tibetan polity to 1032 if another page says the Liugu held Liangzhou after the Uyghur ousting; (2) Li Jiqian's death is 6 January 1004 on the Timeline and 26 January 1004 on his own page, and neither says where he fell, so the 1004 end of the 1003 occupation is confidence 2; (3) the Guiyi dossier has Liangzhou slip to nobody in 881-882 and the Tibetan dossier's 861/863 Liangzhou entries differ, so 882-906 is unsettled and the dossier starts in 906; (4) the Western Xia dossier of ea-05 is the Tangut counterpart for 1003 and 1015 (Dingnan Jiedushi on the Timeline; the dingnan-circuit dossier ends in 990); (5) Tsongkha (Qingtang) is named as a successor on the page and has no dossier. Wuwei is a gazetteer place.
